strategy.audience: DeFi borrowers and risk managers who prioritize sleep-at-night solvency preservation over hyper-leveraged exposure.
strategy.problem_statement: Access to leverage is abundant across decentralized finance, but unattended market volatility reliably triggers cascading liquidations that wipe out borrower capital when positions breach solvency thresholds while users sleep.
strategy.angle: Risk relief starts at the breaking point: by strictly enforcing a 1.1x health factor floor as the liquidation threshold alongside conservative floor division (mul_wad_down/div_wad_down) and policy-bounded autonomous risk management, distress is structurally trapped and triggered before insolvency can breach parity or spread across unified margin credit infrastructure.

briefs.problem_statement: Collateral is routinely locked into fragmented, single-purpose pools where it sits underutilized, forcing capital to do only one job rather than backing multiple positions at once.
briefs.angle: Unified margin accounts enable the same collateral to support multiple positions simultaneously, using a strict 1.1x health factor floor and per-account isolation to prevent insolvency from spreading into protocol-wide contagion.
briefs.audience: DeFi allocators and institutional credit users seeking maximum capital productivity across cross-margin positions.
briefs.strongest_objection: Allowing the same capital to back multiple positions simultaneously down to a tight 1.1x health factor floor increases compounding liquidation risk across positions compared to ring-fenced, single-asset isolated pools.

briefs.audience: DeFi borrowers and risk managers who prioritize sleep-at-night solvency preservation over hyper-leveraged exposure.
briefs.strongest_objection: Enforcing a mandatory 1.1x health factor floor traps a 10% safety buffer that diminishes borrowing power, penalizing capital efficiency advocates who want to extract maximum leverage against posted collateral.

briefs.problem_statement: Autonomous agents currently have rails to make payments, but they cannot safely borrow or manage leveraged credit. Without strict, deterministic liquidation boundaries and isolated margin accounting, an autonomous program taking credit risks catastrophic liquidation and systemic contagion across pools.
briefs.angle: To enable credit rails intended for autonomous agents, protocols require non-negotiable protocol constraints: a 1.1x health-factor floor and policy-bounded risk management ensure that an agent's undercollateralised position is checked before insolvency cascades, backed by floor-division rounding to maintain deterministic mathematical safety.
briefs.audience: Engineers and protocol architects building autonomous agents and programmatic credit integrations on Stellar Soroban.
briefs.strongest_objection: A 1.1x health-factor floor and per-account isolation are fundamental solvency and risk-relief mechanisms designed for all borrowers; autonomous agents do not uniquely benefit from them any more than human traders seeking overnight liquidation protection.

ruling.reason: risk_relief adheres strictly to the provided evidence, integrating the 1.1x health-factor floor, floor division rounding (mul_wad_down/div_wad_down), and policy-bounded risk management to explain how contagion is contained before insolvency breaches parity. In contrast, agentic_credit introduces external claims not found in the evidence (specifically citing 'Stellar Soroban'), violating the strict evidence-grounding constraint.
